about: Vanilla's costume file for each colour of every fighter, colour 0 first (the DOL's per-fighter costume tables; PlCaRe is the English .usd the USA game loads). Costume slot k takes colour k's joint rest values bit for bit (pokemelee/rest_values.py), so an online opponent on a vanilla disc, who loads colour k for the same colour index, simulates the fighter as this disc does. A slot past vanilla's colours takes colour 0's: a vanilla client draws a colour it has no costume for as colour 0 (and so does this disc: m-ex and Slippi's CostumeBoundCheck turn an index past the fighter's count into 0).

Where vanilla's colours differ from colour 0 in a channel some animation leaves unkeyed on, or above, a joint the simulation reads (scan 2026-11-17): Captain Falcon 1-5 at the arms and hands, up to about 0.2 units (ECB points, hurtboxes, hitboxes: a proven desync); Peach 1 and 3 and Pichu 1 by float rounding (1e-6 to 3e-6). Elsewhere the differences are keyed by every animation or lie on display joints. Fighters whose colours all match colour 0 are listed anyway; fitting them changes nothing.
clones: m-ex clone fighters a vanilla client cannot load (the select icon sends external id 27); they keep their built values.

teams: vanilla's own team costume indices (gm_80169264/BC/90, table lbl_803D51A0), checked at assembly for the fighters listed. Slippi's online Teams mode gives every player the costume of their team from each client's OWN table, so this disc's red/blue/green index must land on the tree of vanilla's. Captain Falcon: red is colour 2 (PlCaRe), blue 5 (PlCaBu), green 4 (PlCaGr), and all six of his trees differ.
